title: Lattice Join
alt: The lattice engine resolves profiles and facets into an effective policy, then project overrides apply.
text: Boxes: Defaults (DefaultPolicy), Profiles (.config/archetypes/*.yaml), Facets (.config/archetypes/facets/*.yaml), External (Fleet, Org, Workstation), Repository (Complexity Overrides), Audit Compat (builtin:audit-compat-v1), Lattice Engine (ResolvePolicy), Control Overrides (Branch & Supply Chain), Resolved Policy (EffectivePolicy), Consumers (audits, plans & workstation config).
Audit Compat → Lattice Engine → Resolved Policy.
Scenario 1, default values: DefaultPolicy provides the baseline. DefaultPolicy sets govet, common-utils, SLSA 1, and independent ReviewMode.
Scenario 2, profile values: A profile sets baseline governance for a stack. native-gpu-systems sets memory bounds, SLSA level 3, and linters.
Scenario 3, facet values: Facets add cross-cutting modifiers. A security facet enforces linear history, signed commits, and security linters.

Scenario 4, join stricter value: The Join keeps the strictest value per dimension. Profiles and facets are joined. Complexity caps take the lowest positive bound. Reviewer count and SLSA level take the maximum. Booleans keep true. Lists are deduplicated unions. strict_ban wins for error_unwraps. ReviewMode keeps the stricter mode (independent) when both sides are known, but passes through an unknown/invalid mode unchanged so validation catches it later.

Scenario 5, overrides relative to join: Project overrides apply on top of the joined policy. ApplyOverrides keeps monotonic strictness for branch protection and supply chain, except for ReviewMode which can be explicitly relaxed.
Scenario 6, resolved policy: The resulting effective policy drives gating. The unified policy is consumed by standardsctl audits, adoption plans, devcontainers, and workstation environments.
Complexity caps take the lowest positive bound. Reviewer count and SLSA level take the maximum. Booleans keep true, lists are deduplicated unions, and strict_ban wins for error_unwraps.
Exception: ReviewMode keeps the stricter mode (independent) when both sides are known, but passes through an unknown/invalid mode unchanged so validation catches it later.
